== Left off the list ==
The list takes only people whose own preserved sources give a Decipher staff title, "of Decipher", "Decipher's" or "Decipher Inc.". These pages were checked and left off:
* [[Jonathan Quesenberry]]: the Squadron table places Red Leader at Decipher Inc., and he hosted [[Radio Free Decipher]] broadcast 10 (March 1999). No preserved Decipher source gives him a staff title. The ''Jedi Knights'' rulebook lists him under Special Thanks.
* [[Jason Winter]]: his staff dates (February 1996 – January 1998) come from a 2025 YouTube interview with no preserved copy, and the fan anagram page calls him a "Decipherian". The ''Jedi Knights'' rulebook lists him as a playtester.
* [[Mike Gray]] and [[Becky Higgerson]]: only the fan anagram page ("Decipherian"). Higgerson is also on the ''Jedi Knights'' team list.
* [[Cindy Thornburg]]: Wikipedia names her among Decipher's key people; the ''Jedi Knights'' team list names her with no role. No preserved Decipher source gives a title.
* [[Calvin Sanders]]: Decipher's 1997 Special Events page says he and [[Dale Maurice]] programmed the [[Star Wars CCG Palace]]; it does not say he was on staff.
* [[Trevor Hinkley]]: billed as a "Decipher intern" on Radio Free Decipher broadcast 123 (April 2002); an internship, not staff.
* [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]]: designed SWCCG through Technical Game Services, their own company.
* [[Kathy Lischke]]: covered [[DecipherCon 1999]] on Decipher's event board and playtested ''Jedi Knights''.
* ''Jedi Knights'' team credit only, with no role: [[Rich Loftus]], [[Anthony Vittone]], [[Rick Eddleman]], [[Walt Eley]], [[Ryan Honeyman]], [[Jennifer Gilbert]], [[Matt Holland]], [[Kurt Luchtman]], [[Lisa Brinn]], [[Faye Holt]], [[Liz Duffey]], [[Roland Williams]], [[Dominiek Vermandere]].
* Volunteers and writers, not employees on their sources: [[Kim Burns]] (volunteer) and [[Richard Handley]] (''Star Wars Insider'' writer).
* [[John Kaufeld]] and [[Jean-Luc Simard]] (DecipherCon 2000 contributing writers), [[Jim Colson]] and [[Arthur Wright]] (Squadron Members), and [[Brianna Emery]] (attendee).
* No page yet: Jeff Snyder (''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG developer with [[Michael Girard]], 2003), Kathy McCracken (DecipherCon 2002 Daily News writer), Chris McKenna (Star Trek CCG Ambassador).

== Sources for two entries ==
* [[Jerry Darcy]] came to Decipher in April 1995 through Technical Game Services. On Radio Free Decipher broadcast 12 (April 1999), [[Carol Wisely]] said he had been with Decipher about four years as lead designer for Star Wars. See [[Radio Free Decipher/Episode 12 transcript]].
* [[Francis Lalumiere]]: a 1999 Decipher caption calls him a "New addition to the Decipher team", and the ''Jedi Knights'' Design Diary gives his Decipher title, The Juggler.

== Net Reps (2026-10-25) ==
Decipher Net Reps count as Decipher staff, so their pages get [[:Category:Decipher employees]]. That is Bill's call (2026-10-25). [[Mark Tuttle]] stays tagged on that basis.
A scan of every page in [[:Category:People]] found only one other person whose page calls them a Decipher net or internet representative: [[Sandy Wible]]. Her row now lists that role, with the preserved Flashback interview as its source. No other Net Rep has a person page with such a source yet.
